Dolly Parton's legacy is one brimming with love. Her influence has been felt far and wide, so much so that it even showed up at our 2026 United for Working Families Summit last week.
 During his keynote, Eugene Naughton, President of The Dollywood Company, shared, "Dolly has always been an inspiration to me. She's as much a friend as a boss." This loving leadership is evident in the way Dollywood cares for its employees, too.
 From free meals and affordable housing to helping employees pursue a college degree, Dollywood makes it a priority to show up for its workforce with exceptional care.
 From her music to the way she did business, Dolly showed us that success and generosity go hand in hand. Her legacy lives on because of the way she treated people.
 Thank you, Eugene, for sharing a bit of Dolly's unifying love with us last week. As we remember Dolly, we're grateful for the way her legacy continues to inspire all of us to say, "I see you," and truly mean it.
 For resources to help bring this kind of care into your own workplace, visit unitedwaycha.org/workingfamilies.

School is fully back in session and we’re setting out to make school zones even safer, Chattanooga!
 In partnership with Hamilton County Schools, we’ve updated the school zone traffic lights at all 34 public schools within Chattanooga’s city limits. This update has moved the systems away from their older manual use, syncing them all to be automated through a pre-programmed schedule for bell times, including known school holidays and in-service days. Our tech team can even control them through the Traffic Management Center in the event of emergency closures or late/early starts. 
 Enjoy these quick safety tips from Mike Griffith — we hope everyone has a wonderful school year!

items.content_text:
When we think about historic preservation, we often think first about buildings. But some of the most important things we inherit from the past can’t be preserved with bricks and mortar.
 Preserve Chattanooga has been teaching historic preservation at UTC for many years. Dollywood is used as an example of intangible cultural heritage, the traditions, knowledge, skills, music, stories, crafts, and customs that are passed from one generation to the next.
 Throughout Dollywood, Appalachian culture is expressed through traditional music, foods, storytelling, craftsmanship, and demonstrations by artisans practicing skills that have deep roots in the region. Blacksmithing, woodworking, quilting, instrument making, traditional cooking, gospel and bluegrass music—these are forms of heritage every bit as meaningful as a historic building.
 Of course, Dollywood is a modern theme park and a commercial enterprise, but that is part of what makes it such an interesting example for students. Preservation doesn't always mean freezing something in time. Cultural traditions survive because people practice them, teach them, adapt them, and find ways to make them relevant to new generations.
 That is an important lesson for historic preservation: sometimes we preserve a place; sometimes we preserve the knowledge, traditions, and stories that give a place meaning. And sometimes, if we do it well, we preserve both.
 Thank you, Dolly Parton, for sharing the heritage of a region so well!

items.content_text:
Chattanooga Police Department’s Drone First Responder Pilot Program Takes Off
 CPD announced today the launch of its Drone First Responder (DFR) Pilot Program, designed to provide officers and other first responders with real-time information about active incidents and other emergency calls for service. The program is intended to help officers make faster, more informed decisions, improve resource deployment, and enhance overall public safety. 
 The program consists of two prepositioned unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) located at Chattanooga Fire Department Stations 4 and 9. These locations were selected based on data identifying areas where violent crime most frequently occurred. 
 When a call for service occurs, the UAS is launched by a police officer located in the CPD Real Time Intelligence Center (RTIC) and flies to the scene of the call. Once on scene, the drone transmits live video to responding officers, operators, and incident commanders.
 The drones are not used for routine patrols or general surveillance. CPD’s Unmanned Aircraft System policy prohibits the department and its officers from using drones for general surveillance, harassing individuals or groups, or conducting business not law enforcement-generated or affiliated. Every deployment is governed by federal regulations, department policy, and publicly reported.  
 An online dashboard provides information on CPD’s DFR pilot program including flight maps, duration, call types, and date/time. This can be found on the Drone First Responder page on https://hubs.la/Q04vp-D80. Data obtained by the UAS shall be retained in accordance with CPD policies: OPS-63, Digital Recording Systems and SOP-22, Digital Evidence.
 The DFR drones and associated equipment are manufactured by BRINC, an American technology company specializing in drones and software for public safety and emergency response. Officer training and DFR test flights began in late April and the pilot program is now fully operational.
 #CPDNews

At UTC, research is moving beyond the labs and classrooms to reach local communities, helping stakeholders better understand their needs and challenges.
 Dr. Hemant Jain, director of the Journey Health Foundation Research Center and the MS Data Analytics Program, is leading work that uses data analysis to identify the root causes of health and economic inequities across the region.
 The center recently announced 10 projects in partnership with local nonprofits, supporting UTC faculty as they explore issues ranging from healthcare access and 911 calls to food deserts and community outreach.
 In the latest “Behind the Research at UTC,” Jain discusses the center’s work, his interest in healthcare research and opportunities for students to get involved.

Many of tomorrow’s problem-solvers may be sitting in classrooms right now.
 Are we preparing them to reach their potential? 
 The OECD's Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) is the world's largest survey of 15-year-old students.
 It helps us understand if education systems are preparing young people with the skills and attitudes they need to tackle the world's biggest challenges.
 This year's PISA focuses on science, as well as other indicators such as curiosity, persistence and self-directed learning.
 Hear from AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio on why science education matters not only for future scientists, but for everyone learning to understand and adapt to a changing world.
 The latest results of PISA will be released: 
 📅 8 September 2026 | 9:30 CEST / 07:30 UTC 
 Watch the release live: https://brnw.ch/21x5e7k 
 #OECDPISA

Wilson.  
 A dedicated public servant, Judge Wilson was first elected as City of Collegedale Court Judge in 1990 and served faithfully until his passing on January 9, 2026. Known for his fairness and steady presence on the bench, he left a lasting mark on the Collegedale community.  
 "Judge Wilson gave so much of himself to this community and this court," said Collegedale Municipal Court Clerk Rachel Shuttles. "This dedication is a chance for all of us who knew him, and everyone he served, to come together in his honor." 
 The ceremony will give the community an opportunity to reflect on Judge Wilson’s legacy and celebrate his years of service to the City of Collegedale. A reception with light refreshments will follow.

items.title: How do tax-benefit systems impact people’s life satisfaction?  Our latest paper, supported via #TSI, explores how tax‑be...
items.content_text:
How do tax-benefit systems impact people’s life satisfaction? 
 Our latest paper, supported via #TSI, explores how tax‑benefit systems play a significant role in shaping differences in people’s subjective well‑being across European countries.  
 The findings show that while higher taxes alone are associated with lower life satisfaction, citizens in countries with effective governments experience higher overall life satisfaction.  
 It also reveals that lower-income households tend to report higher life satisfaction when they receive more support through benefit, while   higher-income households that pay more taxes report only slightly lower life satisfaction.
 This suggests that inclusive tax-benefit systems can enhance overall life satisfaction if accompanied by good governance quality. 
 Discover the more insights: https://brnw.ch/21x5ds9

items.content_text:
She came from a little cabin
 beneath the Great Smoky Mountains.
 And somehow,
 she made the whole world feel like home.
 She carried Tennessee in her voice.
 In her stories.
 In her kindness.
 In every song she ever sang.
 She showed the world our mountains.
 Our music.
 Our humor.
 Our heart.
 And no matter how far she went,
 she never really left.
 Because Dolly belonged to the world.
 But she was always ours.
 Today, Tennessee feels a lot quieter.
 The mountains, a little emptier.
 But we know her voice will echo here forever.
 We will always love you, Dolly.
 Photo: Alan Mayor

items.content_text:
Thank you, Dolly. 🤍
Global icon and humanitarian, Dolly Parton, known to the world as a beloved singer, songwriter, philanthropist, actress, playwright, and author died peacefully today in Nashville, Tennessee. She was 80 years old.
 Dolly is preceded in death by her beloved husband of 59 years Carl Thomas Dean (1942 – 2025), her mother Avie Lee Caroline Owens (1923 – 2003), and father, Robert Lee Parton, Sr. (1921 – 2000). 
 A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family. Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact.
 At Dolly’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family. Dolly’s fans and friends from around the world are encouraged to pay tribute to Dolly on social media by tagging @DollyParton or by leaving a message at www.dollyparton.com         
 In lieu of flowers the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library at www.imaginationlibrary.com

 Hamilton County, TN – On August 24, at around 10 p.m., an HCSO Lieutenant observed a motorcycle traveling at a high rate of speed on US-27 North and activated their vehicle’s emergency equipment to conduct a traffic stop. The pursuit was terminated after visual of the bike was lost; however, a short time later it was spotted by an HCSO Sergeant and an HCSO traffic investigator at the ramp from Highway 153 onto Shepherd Road, where they successfully stopped the suspect and took him into custody.
 The suspect was identified as a 17-year-old male juvenile, and the bike was registered to the suspect’s father. Upon inspection of the bike, it was found that the suspect had covered the entire license plate with black tape.
 The suspect is being charged with:
 - Felony Evading Arrest
 - Speeding
 - Reckless Driving
 - Improper Display of a Tag
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

items.content_text:
Governments widely use tax incentives to attract and shape investment.
 When well designed and implemented, tax incentives can support investment policy goals, but the evidence on their performance in practice is mixed.
 Tax incentives are not always effective at achieving policy goals and can generate significant costs and economic distortions.
 The #OECD Investment Tax Incentives Database (ITID) compiles data on investment tax incentives across over 70 emerging and developing economies. This work enables cross-country comparisons and enhances the analysis of policy impacts.
 Early insights show that corporate income tax exemptions remain the most widely used instrument, despite often limited effectiveness.
 Meanwhile, well-designed expenditure-based incentives can more directly support new investment but are less used.
 Explore the data here ➡️ https://brnw.ch/21x5chy

items.content_text:
Exploring Downtown: The Dwell Hotel
 Did you know one of Downtown Chattanooga's most vibrant hotels sits on historic ground?
 Long before The Dwell Hotel, this site was home to Fort James, a Civil War fortification built to protect Chattanooga. In 1909, the property entered a new chapter when architect L.A. Hirtzfield designed the Colonial Hotel, welcoming travelers during a new era of rapid growth. Later, the hotel would change hands and become known as the Stone Fort Inn, a name that harkened back to the site's origins. 
 In 2016, a new series of renovations were completed, and The Dwell Hotel opened to the public. Today, this corner of East 10th Street is still welcoming visitors, just with a little more color and mid-century modern flair.

items.content_text:
What stories change the dominant narrative?
 We invite local artists and creatives to participate in The People’s Gallery, a month-long exhibition exploring Chattanooga’s grassroots histories of labor, civil rights, racial justice, white supremacy, resistance, and community power.
 The exhibition builds on The People’s History Tour. A foundation for understanding the people who organized, resisted, cared for one another and changed the course of our city. But history is never finished, and no single tour or exhibition can tell the whole story.
 That is where artists come in.
 We’re inviting artists to help us uncover, question and carry forward the stories that have been overlooked, erased, misunderstood or left unfinished.
 There are two ways to participate:
 1️⃣ THE PEOPLE’S HISTORY POSTER COMPETITION
 Submit a portfolio by September 4 for the chance to be selected as one of three artists creating an original 12 × 18" poster responding to the question: What stories change the dominant narrative? Three artists will compete for $2,000 in prizes, with the winning designs unveiled at The People’s Gallery event on October 24.
 2️⃣ THE PEOPLE’S GALLERY EXHIBITION
 Submit existing or original work exploring the themes of The People’s Gallery for inclusion in our month-long exhibition at Stove Works this October. Submissions are due September 18.
 Learn more and apply: calebcha.org/peoples-gallery
 Artists are encouraged to honor what is theirs to tell and the boundaries of others.
 We want to see the stories that deserve to be seen, heard, remembered, questioned and carried forward.

 CHATTANOOGA, Tenn. -- The Chattanooga Police Department (CPD) Traffic/DUI Unit was informed by the Hamilton County Medical Examiner's Office that a driver from an August 17, 2026 crash died from the injuries she sustained. The two-vehicle crash occurred near 7100 Shallowford Road within the intersection of the Interstate 75 exit ramp. 
 Through investigation, interview, and observation CPD's Traffic/DUI investigators determined Vehicle 1 (Ford Edge) was exiting I-75 Northbound when, for unknown reasons, it drove through a red light and collided with Vehicle 2 (Toyota Avalon). 
 Hamilton County EMS transported the driver of Vehicle 1 to a local hospital. The driver of Vehicle 2 sustained minor injuries and was not taken to a hospital. CPD was notified that the driver of Vehicle 1, a 73-year-old woman, succumbed to her injuries on August 22, 2026.

COLLEGEDALE COMMISSION INVESTS IN POLICE STAFFING
 COLLEGEDALE, TN (08/24/2026) - The Collegedale Police Department has hired four additional police officers, increasing the department’s full-time sworn strength from 29 to 33 officers.
 The new positions were made possible through the continued support of the Collegedale City Commission and its commitment to investing in public safety, officer safety, and the level of service provided to the community.
 “We are grateful to the members of the Collegedale City Commission for recognizing the importance of maintaining appropriate staffing as our community continues to grow and change,” Police Chief Jack Sapp said. “Their support allows us to strengthen our department, provide our officers with additional resources and backup, and continue delivering the level of service Collegedale residents expect.”
 All four new officers will be assigned to the Patrol Division, increasing patrol staffing from 19 to 23 officers. Patrol officers provide the department’s around-the-clock response to calls for service, traffic safety, neighborhood and business patrols, crash investigations, and other public safety needs throughout the city.
 The additional officers will improve the department’s ability to maintain consistent patrol coverage when personnel are unavailable because of training, vacation, illness, court appearances, or other obligations. The increased staffing will also provide greater flexibility for officer backup, proactive policing, traffic safety, and community engagement.
 The department’s responsibilities extend beyond Collegedale’s residential population. Each day, thousands of additional people enter the city to work, attend school, shop, visit businesses, and travel through the community. The additional officers will help the department meet those demands while maintaining a strong public safety presence throughout Collegedale.
 “The City Commission’s decision is an investment not only in the people who live, work, attend school, and travel through Collegedale, but also in the men and women who serve this community around the clock,” Sapp said. “These additional officers will strengthen officer safety and help us continue providing professional, responsive service to our community.”
 The Collegedale Police Department extends its sincere appreciation to the Collegedale City Commission for recognizing the department’s staffing needs and taking meaningful action to support the officers who serve the community.

items.content_text:
HCSO Recovers Gun from Ooltewah High School, Juvenile Charged
 Hamilton County, TN – On the morning of August 24, 2026, HCSO K-9 Unit deputies responded to Ooltewah High School to assist the assigned school resource deputy (SRD) and the school’s administration with a report of a potential firearm on campus.
 An HCSO K-9 alerted to a vehicle in the school’s parking lot, initiating a search that recovered a loaded firearm, magazine, and multiple additional rounds of ammunition.
 A juvenile suspect was taken into custody and charged with the following: 
 • Possession of a Firearm on School Property
 This is an example of the important partnership that the HCSO and Hamilton County Department of Education have in ensuring the safety of our students.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

items.content_text:
Connecting people with opportunity is at the heart of workforce development.

Recently, members of our workforce development team, Lauri Wilson and Gloria Freeman, attended the Athens Job Fair, connecting with job seekers and 20 other employers from across the region.

For someone looking for their next opportunity, knowing where to start can make all the difference. Our team shared resources available through the local workforce system, including job search assistance through JOBS4TN, resume development, career counseling, job readiness support, and information about WIOA Title I education and training opportunities for eligible participants.

This is an important part of the work happening through SETD that we look forward to sharing more about: connecting people to careers, helping employers find talent, and strengthening Southeast Tennessee’s workforce one connection at a time.

We’re proud of our workforce team for continuing to meet people where they are and connect them with the tools and opportunities to move forward!

🚧📹 New Technology Alert! Better Stormwater Protection for Red Bank! 🌧️
 The City of Red Bank's Public Works Stormwater Division is excited to put their new pipe inspection camera into service, giving our team a safer and more efficient way to inspect underground stormwater infrastructure!
 This past Friday, the stormwater team met with City Manager Martin Granum, Mayor Stephanie Dalton, and Public Works Director Greg Tate to demonstrate the new capabilities that this device offers. With this new camera, the team will be able to inspect underground stormwater assets quickly and safely, helping to ensure that the stormwater system is ready to weather future storms.
 By allowing crews to identify blockages, structural concerns, and other issues without extensive excavation, this technology will help improve maintenance efforts and protect critical infrastructure throughout our community.
 If you see the stormwater division team members on the side of the road using this camera, please give them space to work safely and proceed with caution around their work zone.
 Investing in modern equipment helps our team work smarter, safer, and more effectively as we continue to serve the citizens of Red Bank. 💙
 #RedBankTN #PublicWorks #StormwaterManagement

items.title: Final stop on our #NationalAviationWeek journey throughout CHA history: the early 2020s✨ In 2020, we built our first par...
items.content_text:
Final stop on our #NationalAviationWeek journey throughout CHA history: the early 2020s✨ In 2020, we built our first parking garage. A few years later, we expanded the terminal with a new concourse, including two additional gates, a larger TSA area, a business center, an additional restaurant, a gift shop and more.
 Things have already changed since these photos were taken, too! We've welcomed additional renovations and additions in 2025 and 2026, with more still to come.
 From the 1930s all the way to today, it's been a wonderful journey with our community🫶 Thanks for following along as we traveled through the decades for National Aviation Week✈️

items.title: From creating quality jobs to respecting human rights, responsible business conduct (RBC) is about making sure that the...
items.content_text:
From creating quality jobs to respecting human rights, responsible business conduct (RBC) is about making sure that the activities of businesses and investors are aligned with the needs of society, today and in the future. RBC is essential to building resilient societies, supply chains and economies.
 How is RBC being taken up in company practices and government policies?
 The #OECD Responsible Business Outlook shows that less than 2 in 10 companies have formal processes in place to assess human rights complaints and less than 1 in 10 companies engage with stakeholders on human rights issues.
 What can governments do to increase the uptake of responsible business practices? 
 Read the report to find out ➡️ https://brnw.ch/21x5944
 #OECDResponsibleBusinessConduct
